root_cause: The cancel handler for modal dialogs calls _triggerBackdropTransition when keyboard:false, which may cause side effects. Additionally, the keydown handler for Escape does not prevent the keydown event for modal dialogs when keyboard:false, allowing the native dialog to fire a cancel event that becomes non-cancelable after multiple presses.
repair_strategy: Remove the _triggerBackdropTransition call in the cancel handler when keyboard:false. Also, modify the keydown handler to prevent the Escape keydown event for modal dialogs when keyboard:false, so the native cancel event is not fired.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer dismiss the dialog when keyboard:false, allowing users to remain focused on the OTP input and complete the transfer without unexpected loss of focus.
functional_risks: Removing _triggerBackdropTransition eliminates the visual 'bounce' feedback for Escape when keyboard:false, but this feedback was unnecessary because Escape should be inert.
The keydown handler change may affect non-modal dialogs, but the condition ensures non-modal dialogs still work as before.
verification_requirements: Confirm that with keyboard:false, pressing Escape any number of times leaves the dialog open and focus retained in the OTP field.
Confirm that with keyboard:true, pressing Escape once closes the dialog.
Confirm that the Cancel and Send buttons continue to work as expected.
Confirm that backdrop clicks with backdrop:'static' still trigger the bounce transition and do not close the dialog.
